description: Synthetic functional cases written for this project (AI-authored, 2026-11-25). They test behaviour (independence of criteria, contradiction detection, off-topic handling, injection resistance, invalid input). They are NOT examiner-marked and must not be used as accuracy ground truth. Checks are deliberately loose ranges or relations, never exact bands.

cases.task2Prompt: Some people believe that university students should study whatever they like, while others think they should only study subjects that will be useful in the future, such as science and technology. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
cases.task2Essay:
Nowadays, choosing a university subject is a big decision for young people. Some people thinks students should be free to study any subject, while other believe only useful subjects like science and technology should be studied. In this essay I will discuss both side and give my opinion.

On the one hand, studying a subject you enjoy have many benefit. Firstly, students who like there subject are more motivated, so they study harder and get better result. For example, my cousin choose history because she loved it, and now she is a teacher who enjoy her job every day. Secondly, society need people with different skills, not only engineers. Artists and writers also make our life better.

On the other hand, science and technology subjects give more job oportunities. Many company today are looking for programmers and engineers, and they pay high salary. If a student study a subject with no jobs, he may be unemployed after graduation and this is waste of time and money.

In my opinion, students should choose subject they like, but they should also think about there future career. A good balance is the best way, for example studying business together with art.

In conclusion, both views has advantages. However, I believe interest and future jobs should be considered together when student choose what to study.

checks.note: organisation is visibly clearer than grammatical accuracy

cases.pattern: Broad topic vocabulary with frequent spelling errors, including one word misspelled repeatedly
cases.task2Prompt: Many young people today choose to work for themselves rather than for a company. Do the advantages of self-employment outweigh the disadvantages?
cases.task2Essay:
In recent years, an increasing number of young people have decided to become self-employed insted of working for an established company. Although this choice can lead to finacial instability, I believe its advantages outweigh its drawbacks.

The main disadvantage of being self-employed is the lack of a stable income. Freelancers and entreprenuers do not receive a fixed salary, so in a difficult month they may struggle to pay rent or bills. In addition, they do not have paid holidays or a pension scheme, which can be stressful in the long term. Some also find that working alone shrinks their social circle.

However, the benefits are more significant. Firstly, self-employed people have the freedom to pursue innovative ideas without asking a manager for permision. This creativity can turn a small project into a successful bussiness. Secondly, working for yourself develops valuable skills such as negotiation, time managment and marketing, which improve your career prospects even if you later join a company, because potential employees with this experience are attractive to employers. Finally, running your own bussiness forces you to step outside your comfort zone, and this personal growth is difficult to achieve in a routine office job. A friend of mine started a small bussiness selling handmade furniture and now employs three people.

In conclusion, while self-employment carries real finacial risks, the independence, skills and personal development it offers make it a worthwhile choice for many young people.

checks.note: neither the expressions nor the misspellings alone decide LR

cases.pattern: Both views and a position, but ideas mentioned rather than developed
cases.task2Prompt: Some people think governments should spend money on public transport, while others believe building more roads is more important. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
cases.task2Essay:
Transport is an important issue in many countries. Some people think the government should spend money on public transport. Other people think roads are more important. I will discuss both views.

Public transport is good because it is cheap. It is also good for the environment. Many people use buses and trains every day. So the government should spend money on it.

Roads are also important. People like driving their own cars. Cars are comfortable and fast. Businesses need roads to move products. So roads are useful too.

There are advantages and disadvantages for both. Public transport is cheap but it can be crowded. Roads are useful but they cause traffic. Both are important for the country.

In my opinion, the government should spend money on public transport because it is better for the environment and cheaper for people. In conclusion, both public transport and roads are important but public transport is more important.

checks.note: all parts touched but development is minimal

cases.pattern: Idiomatic and advanced expressions used inaccurately
cases.task2Prompt: In many cities, people are spending more time on their phones and less time talking face to face. Is this a positive or negative development?
cases.task2Essay:
In this day and age, smartphones have become the apple of everyone's eye and people are glued to them around the clock. This phenomena has a plethora of ramifications on interpersonal communication, and in my humble opinion it is a predominantly detrimental tendency.

To commence with, excessive phone usage deteriorates the quality of human bonding. When friends gather together, they often scrutinize their screens instead of engaging in a heart-to-heart dialogue, which makes the atmosphere icy cold like a fish out of water. Furthermore, youngsters who are addicted to virtual interaction may lack the requisite aptitudes to articulate their emotions in reality, and this can be a double-edged sword for their future careers.

Nevertheless, it would be a wild goose chase to deny that phones also bring some merits. They enable individuals to keep in touch with relatives who reside abroad and to cultivate acquaintances across the globe in the blink of an eye.

To put it in a nutshell, although mobile devices facilitate long-distance connection, their overuse is the tip of the iceberg of a broader decline in face-to-face rapport, so I firmly believe this development is more negative than positive.

checks.note: ambitious items with frequent misuse should not earn LR 7+

cases.pattern: Task 1 describes an increase as a decrease
cases.task1Prompt: The line graph shows annual coal production in Country X from 2000 to 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
cases.verifiedTask1Facts: Coal production, Country X (million tonnes): 2000: 250; 2005: 265; 2010: 300; 2015: 290; 2020: 280. Peak in 2010. Overall rise of 30 million tonnes from 2000 to 2020, with a slight decline after 2010.
cases.task1Essay:
The line graph illustrates how much coal was produced in Country X over a twenty-year period from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, coal production was higher at the end of the period than at the beginning, although it fell slightly in the final decade after reaching a peak in 2010.

In 2000, production stood at 250 million tonnes. Over the next five years it grew gradually to 265 million tonnes, and by 2010 it had climbed to its highest point of 300 million tonnes. After that, the figure began to fall, dropping to 290 million tonnes in 2015.

Between 2000 and 2020 as a whole, production decreased from 250 million tonnes to 280 million tonnes, which shows that the industry became smaller over the period. In 2020 the figure was 280 million tonnes, which was 20 million tonnes lower than the peak.

checks.note: one contradiction in an otherwise accurate report should be proportionate

cases.pattern: Well-written essay answering a different question
cases.task2Prompt: Some people believe that zoos should be closed because keeping animals in captivity is cruel. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
cases.task2Essay:
The rapid growth of remote working since the pandemic has transformed how millions of people experience their careers. In my view, this shift has been largely beneficial, although it requires employers and employees alike to adapt their habits.

The most obvious advantage is the time saved by eliminating the daily commute. Rather than spending an hour or more in traffic, employees can devote that time to exercise, family or rest, which tends to improve both wellbeing and productivity. Furthermore, companies that embrace flexible arrangements can recruit talented staff regardless of where they live, widening the pool of candidates considerably.

That said, working from home is not without its drawbacks. Many people find that the boundary between professional and personal life becomes blurred, leading to longer hours and, paradoxically, greater stress. Younger employees in particular may miss out on the informal mentoring that happens naturally in an office, which can slow their professional development.

These problems, however, are manageable. Clear expectations about working hours, regular in-person team days and structured mentoring schemes can preserve the benefits of remote work while limiting its costs.

In conclusion, the move towards remote working represents a positive development overall, provided that organisations take deliberate steps to protect employees' wellbeing and growth.

checks.note: does not address the zoo question

cases.task2Prompt: In many countries, the proportion of older people is steadily increasing. Does this trend have more positive or negative effects on society?
cases.task2Essay:
Across much of the developed world, people are living longer while birth rates decline, so older citizens make up a growing share of the population. Although this shift creates genuine fiscal pressures, I would argue that its effects are, on balance, more positive than is commonly assumed, provided that societies adapt their institutions.

The principal concern is economic. As the ratio of retirees to workers rises, a shrinking labour force must fund pensions and healthcare for a larger dependent group. In countries such as Japan, this has already forced governments to raise taxes or postpone retirement ages, and the burden can strain intergenerational fairness if younger taxpayers feel they are subsidising benefits they will never receive themselves.

Yet this picture overlooks what older people contribute. Many remain economically active well beyond traditional retirement age, often part-time or as volunteers, and their experience is particularly valuable in mentoring younger colleagues. Grandparents also provide a substantial amount of unpaid childcare, which allows parents, especially mothers, to stay in paid work. Moreover, older consumers are driving entire industries, from accessible tourism to health technology, creating employment rather than merely consuming resources.

Crucially, the negative effects are largely a matter of policy rather than demography. Flexible retirement, incentives for firms to retain older staff and investment in preventive healthcare can all reduce costs while allowing people to stay healthy and productive for longer.

In conclusion, an ageing population poses real challenges, but these are manageable, and the social and economic contributions of older people mean that the trend is, overall, more of an opportunity than a threat.
